speaker: Doctor
text: I am sorry, but there seems to be a missing response from the patient or their guardian regarding your symptoms. Could you please describe the specific nature of the feeding difficulties and any other symptoms the 8-month-old boy is experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the stools liquid and foul-smelling, or are they small and hard? Have you noticed any vomiting, and if so, is it forceful or projectile? REQUEST TEST: Stool_analysis, Abdominal_ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but I need to see the test results from the ultrasound and stool analysis to confirm the cause of the distension and foul-smelling stools. In the meantime, has the baby passed any gas or stool since the symptoms started, and do you notice any "squirt" when he cries? DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease (if associated with delayed meconium and failure to thrive) or Intussusception (if acute onset with colicky pain). Please wait for the imaging results to finalize the specific diagnosis.
